headline: Seven majors below their 200-day lines, yet short-term momentum and ETF flows are pointing the other way
paragraphs: Start with the map, because it settles the argument about what kind of market this is. Every major in the set, BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE, ADA, sits below its 200-day moving average, and none show a golden cross. BTC is 47.8% off its 12-month high of $124,739.81, ETH is 60.1% off its own, and ADA is furthest out at 79.5% below its peak. That is a broad-based downtrend, not a single asset's problem. When the entire cohort agrees on direction against the long-term average, that's the regime you're trading, whatever the daily candle says.

But the momentum readings tell a quieter story layered on top. RSI-14 is mid-range to firm across most names (BNB 66.0, ADA 66.3, SOL 57.7, ETH 57.2), and MACD sits above its signal line for BTC, SOL, BNB, DOGE, and ADA. ADA in particular is up 16.23% over 7 days and 36.16% over 30, a sharp bounce inside a market still below trend. XRP is the outlier here: RSI 40.9, MACD below signal, down 3.91% over the week. That's a downtrend where momentum has turned up almost everywhere except XRP, worth flagging as a genuine divergence rather than smoothing it into one story.

Positioning adds texture. Funding is positive and annualized in the 8-11% range across BTC, SOL, XRP, and DOGE (ETH is a mild 2.5%), meaning longs are paying to hold their bets on every one of these pairs. Long/short account ratios run hot on the smaller names, XRP at 3.61, DOGE at 4.99, SOL at 2.01, which is a crowded long book on alts even as price momentum firms. The liquidation tape over the last 20-22 hours mostly squeezed shorts (BTC shorts lost $636k versus $139k for longs; ETH shorts lost $2.68M versus $182k for longs), consistent with the bounce. XRP and DOGE flip that pattern, with longs taking the bigger liquidation hit ($327k vs $28k on XRP, $134k vs $4k on DOGE) despite funding running against them too. Crowded and expensive is the right description for those two right now.

On flows, the traditional-finance bid is visible and dated: BTC spot ETFs posted $101.7M net on 07 Aug 2026, with same_direction_days at 5 and a $865.3M net over the last five sessions, a genuinely persistent five-day pull in one direction. ETH ETFs added $49.6M on the same date, $243.7M over five sessions, though same_direction_days sits at 4, one session short of a clean sweep. Whale wallets moved $103,045,101 net off exchanges over the last 48 hours, led by two withdrawals from Kraken totaling roughly $168M against a $65M deposit into Binance. The weekly trend behind that is choppier than the headline number suggests: the last four weekly net figures run -$146.9M, +$445.9M, +$1,075.3M, +$67.2M, so today's outflow sits inside a series that has swung both ways, not a smooth accumulation line. Stablecoin float, the market's dry powder, is down 1.02% over 30 days to $306.2B, a mild contraction rather than a buildup.

Sentiment sits at 31, labeled Fear, though that's actually the upper edge of its own 30-day range of 22 to 33. So the crowd gauge is fearful in name but has been drifting less fearful, while the ETF tape has bought for five straight sessions and momentum has turned up on most majors. That gap between what the gauge says and what the flow data shows is the more interesting fact than either number alone. Total market cap is roughly flat on the day (+0.21%) with BTC dominance at 56.7%, so none of this bounce has reshuffled the cap structure yet. Worth watching from here: whether XRP's momentum divergence resolves in either direction, whether ETH's ETF flow completes a fifth same-direction session, and whether the weekly whale net turns cleanly positive for more than a single week rather than oscillating as it has.
